byKey.hideout_area_13_stage_1_description: Home library with various fiction and popular science books and magazines.
byKey.hideout_area_23_stage_1_description: A well-equipped gym to keep your body in good physical shape.
byKey.hideout_area_19_stage_1_description: The moonshine still allows you to produce strong drinks directly in your Hideout.
byKey.hideout_area_12_stage_1_description: A specially equipped place for shooting firearms. For the convenience of evaluating the shooting results, the range is equipped with metal silhouette popper targets for the close range, and paper targets for the long range.
byKey.hideout_area_12_stage_2_description: An improved range with installed ceiling-mounted target rails with three speed levels.
byKey.hideout_area_12_stage_3_description: An advanced shooting range with installed popper targets and a laptop for configuration. Also allows to start training with random rail targets and poppers, scores are displayed on the laptop monitor.
byKey.hideout_area_14_stage_1_description: A special box where specially hired Scavs drop off various items that they've found.
byKey.hideout_area_27_stage_1_description: A circle drawn in chalk and cluttered with mysterious symbols. Such circles are used by the cultists for their rituals. One wonders what would happen if you put something in the middle of it...?
byKey.hideout_area_26_stage_1_description: A mannequin with a weapon rack. Allows you to prepare a set of equipment for the raid.
byKey.hideout_area_26_stage_2_description: With two mannequins, you can not only prepare gear for a raid, but also display something cool and rare. Would look great.
byKey.hideout_area_26_stage_3_description: Several mannequins with a weapon rack. With a wardrobe like this, it will be easy to store quick access gear for any occasion.
byKey.hideout_area_20_stage_1_description: Basic bitcoin farm of 10 units. Using the computing power of graphics cards, you can use the system to produce physical bitcoins.
byKey.hideout_area_20_stage_2_description: An improved bitcoin farm of 25 units. Using the computing power of graphics cards, you can use the system to produce physical bitcoins.
byKey.hideout_area_20_stage_3_description: Maximum size bitcoin farm for 50 units with water cooling. Using the computing power of graphics cards, you can use the system to produce physical bitcoins.
byKey.hideout_area_5_stage_1_description: A simple barrel with firewood to maintain heat. A very basic option for heating. Dangerous because of toxic carbon monoxide.
byKey.hideout_area_5_stage_2_description: A potbelly stove is a metal stove for interior heating, popular in the first half of the 20th century. An irreplaceable thing in the Hideout, especially when connected to the ventilation system for the output of combustion products.
byKey.hideout_area_5_stage_3_description: Equips the entire Hideout with additional electric heaters. Now, together with the potbelly stove, you won't be afraid of any cold.
byKey.hideout_area_4_stage_1_description: A simple fuel generator that can provide basic Hideout equipment with electricity. The heart of your shelter. Fuel is needed to maintain the working power grid.
byKey.hideout_area_4_stage_2_description: A superior high power generator. It allows you to use a wider range of electrical appliances. Provides additional slots for installing fuel cans.
byKey.hideout_area_4_stage_3_description: Industrial generator to ensure the autonomous operation of production facilities. Also provides additional slots for installing fuel cans.
byKey.hideout_area_0_stage_1_description: Ventilation duct suspended from the ceiling. The air duct passes through part of the room, providing the natural movement of air flows. It is necessary for the installation of "smoky" zones where the output of combustion products is required.
byKey.hideout_area_0_stage_2_description: A basic ventilation duct with additional emergency bunker ventilation system of external airflow. Now, besides the removal of combustion products, there will be fresh air in the Hideout.
byKey.hideout_area_0_stage_3_description: A ventilation duct fitted with electric fans to increase the airflow rate. A complete air circulation system is needed for advanced production and chemical research.
byKey.hideout_area_1_stage_1_description: A basic front door. So that all kinds of fools don't come to pay you a visit. It does not save from drafts and moisture, but it creates the feeling that the Hideout is slowly getting settled.
byKey.hideout_area_1_stage_2_description: An improved entrance hall with a reinforced door, a clothes hanger, and other household items. Can’t kick such a door down with just a single kick.
byKey.hideout_area_1_stage_3_description: An advanced Hideout security system which includes, in addition to an armored bunker door, a video surveillance camera, an intercom system, fire extinguishers, as well as special ties to increase the structural strength of walls and ceiling.
byKey.hideout_UnlockArmorRepair: Unlocks armor repair via repair kits
byKey.hideout_area_2_stage_1_description: A primitive toilet. Any amenities are out of the question. Just a bucket and a litter box to maintain basic sanitation in the Hideout.
byKey.hideout_RepairArmorBonus: Reduces armor repair cost using repair kits
byKey.hideout_area_2_stage_2_description: A basic bathroom with a wooden outhouse type toilet and a washstand, connected to the water supply system. All this raises the level of cleanliness and hygiene in the Hideout.
byKey.hideout_area_2_stage_3_description: An advanced bathroom with a dry closet, a shower and a trash can. Everything you need is connected to the water supply system and provides the most affordable level of personal hygiene.
byKey.hideout_area_7_stage_1_description: The continued availability of medication means greater chances of survival after raids. Several medical storage boxes for basic medical care.
byKey.hideout_area_7_stage_2_description: A medical unit consisting of a table for medicine, a chair and a dropper. The healing process will be faster while you are out of raids.
byKey.hideout_area_7_stage_3_description: A full-fledged Hideout medical laboratory. It has everything you need to treat wounds, create medicines and maintain your good health during these difficult times.
byKey.hideout_area_8_stage_1_description: Food in the Hideout provides you with energy for future raids. A basic nutrition unit with an old fridge and a place to eat allows you to recover your energy faster.
byKey.hideout_area_8_stage_2_description: A nutrition unit with a more modern refrigerator, dining accessories, stove and sink, providing better food. Energy is restored faster.
byKey.hideout_area_8_stage_3_description: A full-fledged kitchen with a comfortable stove, an improved sink, an electric kettle, a microwave and everything necessary for fast and high-quality food cooking outside raids. Can’t violate the diet!
byKey.hideout_area_9_stage_1_description: Rest is very important, especially in the besieged Tarkov environment. A mattress over pallets is the very basic thing which can help PMCs relax after hard battles.
byKey.hideout_area_9_stage_2_description: A place to relax, equipped with a normal bed, bedside table and even an old TV. It creates a feeling of comfort and gives nostalgic memories of a former life.
byKey.hideout_area_9_stage_3_description: A lounge area with a sofa, an LCD TV with a Ployka Station console and a stereo system. It is hard to imagine that such comfort can be organized in an underground bunker when the whole world flies into the abyss.
byKey.hideout_UnlockWeaponRepair: Unlocks weapon repair via repair kits
byKey.hideout_area_10_stage_1_description: Everybody needs a place to work with their tools. A simple workbench allows you to do the basic modifications of your weapon and disassembling various technical parts.
byKey.hideout_RepairWeaponBonus: Reduces weapon repair cost using repair kits
byKey.hideout_area_10_stage_2_description: A workplace equipped with everything necessary for the production of simple ammunition and more complex technical tasks required to improve your hideout.
byKey.hideout_area_10_stage_3_description: A full-fledged table of the gunsmithing master. It allows you to produce more advanced cartridges and engage in high-tech tasks, assembly and disassembly of complex electronic devices and mechanical systems.
byKey.hideout_area_11_stage_1_description: If the generator is the heart of the Hideout, then the intelligence center is its brain. For now, this is just an old table and chair for analyzing various information that can help you escape from Tarkov.
byKey.hideout_area_11_stage_2_description: An advanced intelligence center equipped with a laptop, which has more working space due to an additional table. Thanks to Mechanic, it is connected to an isolated computer network, which remained intact after the EMP strike and isolation of Tarkov.
byKey.hideout_area_11_stage_3_description: A full-fledged intelligence center equipped with computer equipment, radio devices and analytical tools. The escape from Tarkov was never so close.
byKey.hideout_area_15_stage_1_description: Basic lighting with paraffin candles, giving a dim and uneven light.
byKey.hideout_area_15_stage_2_description: Hideout lighting with incandescent bulbs. The illumination is more even and brighter than from the candles.
byKey.hideout_area_15_stage_3_description: Hideout lighting with fluorescent lights provides optimal brightness and uniformity of illumination.
byKey.hideout_area_16_stage_1_description: The Hall of Fame is a special rack where you can put your trophies and collectibles.
byKey.hideout_area_16_stage_2_description: A great rack from IDEA that can very nicely hold all the figurines found in raids and several dogtags taken from PMCs.
byKey.hideout_area_16_stage_3_description: A full-fledged area in the Hideout dedicated to storing items of collectible value.
byKey.hideout_area_17_stage_1_description: Air filtration system, connected to the common ventilation system. It provides the air which is as cleanest from harmful impurities as possible.
byKey.hideout_area_18_stage_1_description: Surface-mounted solar-wind batteries improve the overall Hideout power generation.
byKey.hideout_area_22_stage_1_description: A piece of a wall with swollen paint. Nothing serious, but it might become a problem soon.
byKey.hideout_area_22_stage_2_description: A piece of wall with heavily swollen paint. Water is seeping from the wall. You definitely need to do something about it. Wipe the floor, maybe.
byKey.hideout_area_22_stage_3_description: A piece of wall with heavily swollen paint. Part of the paint fell off. Water is seeping from the wall. There seems to be something behind this wall.
byKey.hideout_area_22_stage_4_description: A wall with a hidden door. You don't know who made it and why, but to open it, you will need tools. Also, another wipe wouldn't hurt.
byKey.hideout_area_22_stage_5_description: The damaged part of the wall turned out to be an entrance to the old hidden room. There is nothing inside but rubbish and a dead body. It will take a lot of effort to put this room in shape.
byKey.hideout_area_22_stage_6_description: A tidied up entrance to the new room.
byKey.hideout_area_24_stage_1_description: A small weapon rack. Simplifies firearm storage and allows to display weapons in a fancy way.
byKey.hideout_area_24_stage_2_description: A medium-sized weapon rack. Simplifies firearm storage and allows to display weapons in a fancy way.
byKey.hideout_area_24_stage_3_description: A large weapon rack. Simplifies firearm storage and allows to display weapons in a fancy way.
byKey.hideout_area_6_stage_1_description: Basic water system for collecting groundwater. Contains several water filters and containers for water purification. One of the most important systems for maintaining life support in the Hideout.
byKey.hideout_area_6_stage_2_description: A sophisticated water collection system with additional pipes, filters, and larger containers. Installation of pumps allows to improve the pressure in the pipes and, consequently, the pressure of water.
byKey.hideout_area_6_stage_3_description: An advanced water collection system for both groundwater and rainwater. It contains various cleaning filters, an electric pump and an extensive water supply system throughout the Hideout. An additional filtration and enrichment system allows you to get very clean and high-quality water.
byKey.55f2d3fd4bdc2d5f408b4567 Description:
The industrial estate and facilities of Chemical Plant No. 16 were rented out illegally to the TerraGroup corporation. During the advent of the Contract Wars, the plant became the scene of numerous firefights between BEAR and USEC that ultimately determined control over the industrial district of Tarkov.

Later on, in the wake of the chaos, the plant facilities became a shelter for the remaining civilians, Scavs, and military operatives, including the scattered remains of the BEAR and USEC contingents.
byKey.6733700029c367a3d40b02af Description: A facility of one of TerraGroup's contractors, Knossos LLC. According to public sources, they build amusement and theme parks. However, this place looks more like a heavily fortified bunker than a new theme park.
byKey.5b0fc42d86f7744a585f9105 Description: Secret underground TerraGroup Labs facility hidden right under the center of Tarkov. Officially, this research center does not exist and, based on data scraps, is engaged in research and development as well as testing and simulation of projects in chemistry, physics, biology, and other high technology.
byKey.69af492a4819ea4ba10a69c5 Description:
In the Gulf of Finland, trapped within the blockade surrounding Tarkov, lies the nuclear-powered icebreaker "Boreas", owned by the logistics corporation Paradigm Shipping. The exact purpose of "Boreas" and the cargo it carries remain unknown. 

It appears that Paradigm Shipping and TerraGroup made special efforts to minimize any mention of the icebreaker in the press and keep its routes and assignments classified.
byKey.5704e3c2d2720bac5b8b4567 Description: The Priozersk Nature Reserve recently became part of the state-protected wildlife reserves of the North-Western Federal District.
byKey.59fc81d786f774390775787e Description:
The industrial estate and facilities of Chemical Plant No. 16 were rented out illegally to the TerraGroup corporation. During the advent of the Contract Wars, the plant became the scene of numerous firefights between BEAR and USEC that ultimately determined control over the industrial district of Tarkov.

Later on, in the wake of the chaos, the plant facilities became a shelter for the remaining civilians, Scavs, and military operatives, including the scattered remains of the BEAR and USEC contingents.
byKey.5704e4dad2720bb55b8b4567 Description: The lighthouse at Cape Dalniy was an important strategic object on the way to Tarkov. During Contract Wars, it was the main entry point for USEC units and served as their base of operations. After the conflict, Scavs took a fancy to this place, until the old owners returned, who decided to stay in Tarkov and establish their own order.
byKey.5704e5fad2720bc05b8b4567 Description: The secret Federal State Reserve Agency base that, according to urban legends, contains enough supplies to last for years: food, medications, and other resources, enough to survive an all-out nuclear war.
byKey.Exit1: Hole in the Wall by the Mountains
byKey.653e6760052c01c1c805532f Description: The business center of Tarkov. This is where TerraGroup was headquartered. This is where it all began.
byKey.5714dc692459777137212e12 Description: Downtown Tarkov houses banks, malls, and hotels, as well as all the other amenities a thriving metropolis could have needed.
byKey.56f40101d2720b2a4d8b45d6 Description: A large area of industrial park land situated adjacent to the factory zone. The area houses a customs terminal, fuel storage facilities, offices, and dorms, as well as a variety of other infrastructure and buildings.
byKey.6a294a5b5eb5f9a1700417b7 Description: Secret underground TerraGroup Labs facility hidden right under the center of Tarkov. Officially, this research center does not exist and, based on data scraps, is engaged in research and development as well as testing and simulation of projects in chemistry, physics, biology, and other high technology.
byKey.65b8d6f5cdde2479cb2a3125 Description: The business center of Tarkov. This is where TerraGroup was headquartered. This is where it all began. The area has yet again become a hot zone since the early days of the conflict.
byKey.5704e554d2720bac5b8b456e Description:
The Shoreline area makes up a large part of the outskirts of Tarkov and is located next to the Port.

The area houses a partially abandoned village, modern private housing, agricultural fields, long stretches of beach, a boating facility, gas station, weather station, and a cellular tower as well as other commercial facilities.

Shoreline's main point of interest is the Azure Coast health resort which consists of several blocks, exclusively powered by a nearby hydroelectric power plant. The resort had previously been used as temporary accommodation for members of TerraGroup and the corporation's associated divisions in preparation for the evacuation of the Tarkov Port.
byKey.68236e8153654e8c1200798a Description: The business center of Tarkov. This is where TerraGroup was headquartered. This is where it all began.
byKey.5714dbc024597771384a510d Description: The South Interchange is a key transport location for the city. This strategic area connects the port and harbor with the industrial outskirts of Tarkov. Located in the center of the interchange is a huge ULTRA shopping mall which was used as the main base of operation for the EMERCOM evacuation.
byKey.65cc8f81a9aac3e77d0cfd3e Description: The southern port Terminal has been under Russian Armed Forces control since the beginning of the Tarkov conflict. After the city was sealed off, the terminal was fortified and became the primary evacuation point, sought by both civilian refugees and PMC units. According to unconfirmed reports, TerraGroup personnel were also evacuated through this port.
byKey.54cb50c76803fa8b248b4571 Description: The Warrant officer in charge of supply warehouses on the sustaining base enforcing the Norvinsk region blockade. Secretly supplied the BEAR PMC operators with weapons, ammunition, and various other provisions he had at his disposal during the Contract Wars.
byKey.54cb57776803fa99248b456e Description: Head of the Trauma Care Department of the Tarkov Central City Hospital.
byKey.579dc571d53a0658a154fbec Description: The conflict had barely started when Fence began setting up anonymous outlets for buying and selling goods. Keeping incognito, he nevertheless managed to put together a well-organised smuggler network, operating all over the Norvinsk region.
byKey.58330581ace78e27b8b10cee Description: Previously a port zone customs terminal employee, who initially oversaw dealings of the terminal's goods. Over the course of the conflict, he put together a gang of thugs in order to grab everything of value that he could lay his hands on in the vicinity of the terminal.
byKey.5935c25fb3acc3127c3d8cd9 Description: UN peacekeeping Force supply officer, based in one of the central checkpoints leading to the Tarkov port zone. The blue helmets have been seen poking their heads into small deals from the very beginning of the conflict, buying everything of value in exchange for western weapons, ammo, and all kinds of military equipment.
byKey.5a7c2eca46aef81a7ca2145d Description: A former chemical plant foreman, who from the very beginning of the conflict took to weapon modification, repairs, and maintenance of complex equipment and technology. He prefers clandestine solo living and operates discreetly, while placing complicated and challenging tasks above all else.
byKey.5ac3b934156ae10c4430e83c Description: Previously, he worked as a director in a shopping center located in the suburbs of Tarkov. Now dealing in mostly clothing- and gear-related items, anywhere from sunglasses to body armor.
byKey.5c0647fdd443bc2504c2d371 Description: Before the conflict, he worked as a hunter in the Priozersk Natural Reserve under the State Hunting Service. A professional hunter and survival specialist. Even now, he still guards the reserve's hunting grounds from various aggressive individuals.
byKey.68fe15990f29ba3fdbba9d55 Description: A multi-function radio station with built-in cryptographic processor.
byKey.6617beeaa9cfa777ca915b7c Description: The Arena host who organizes pit fights across Tarkov.

byKey.6582bd252b50c61c565828e2 Description: A bottle of rare French collector soft wine Le Jean.
byKey.6575a6ca8778e96ded05a802 Description: A random access storage device (information storage device), based on the magnetic recording principle. Contains various compromising data on TerraGroup.
byKey.657acb2ac900be5902191ac9 Description: Cadastral registry records containing data on TerraGroup real estate in Tarkov.
byKey.666073159916667083033cb9 Description: A small diary that had been abandoned by its owner a long time ago. The entries are barely legible due to the rough handwriting.
byKey.666879d498b97e3a8f09f1ae Description: You can argue endlessly that different factories of the same company provide comparable quality, but at the critical moment everyone chooses the original.... Perhaps TerraGroup had special arrangements with the American factory to supply a newer model of LEDX.
byKey.667a8ef464eea5fdef0db135 Description: An issue of a gaming magazine that first wrote about one world-famous shooter game.
byKey.66760b3deb51b08bd40c2b08 Description: A random access storage device (information storage device), based on the magnetic recording principle. Contains stolen user data.
byKey.66687bc89111279d600b5062 Description: In the old days, the symbol of power in large cities was a luxurious key the size of a hand. In Tarkov, this tradition was revived, but the key itself was made smaller. Some say that this is the reason why it was lost: someone attached the souvenir to a bunch of keys by mistake and took it away from the town day celebration.
byKey.66c0b39ca1f68fcc1d0c0cc3 Description: The records in this journal reveal side effects after interacting with TerraGroup's drugs... The factory workers likely were unaware of this "research".
byKey.66c0b90c8398582e4b0c2e27 Description: A RUAF pilot logbook. It's unclear how it ended up in the cockpit of the foreign AS350 helicopter. Either the USECs ran out of their own logbooks, or the BEARs ran out of helicopters.
byKey.669fac549b0ce3feae01a137 Description: There's no telling what was in the tank container. It looks nasty, and smells even worse. TerraGroup must have used these tanks to store precursors for their research.
byKey.66a0e523e749756c920d02d0 Description: Hermetic container for storing various chemicals.
byKey.66a0f0926fee20fa70036da6 Description: A blood sample taken from the body of one of the workers at Chemical Plant No. 16. The bodies are clearly not recent, but the blood has not even dried up. Even the texture is the same as fresh blood.
byKey.66b22630a6b4e5ec7c02cdb7 Description: A case containing various expensive precision tools.
byKey.67499a9669a58fceba104a41 Description: A package that the BTR driver was supposed to deliver to Prapor.
byKey.67499b9b909d2013670a5029 Description: The device is designed to suppress UAV guidance systems. Helps to reliably protect any facility from airborne attacks.
byKey.67499adbeca8acb2d2061634 Description: A delivery from outside the cordon that Prapor is waiting for. Judging by the weight, it feels like it's half-empty.
byKey.67499d4deca8acb2d206163b Description: The device is designed to suppress UAV guidance systems. Helps to reliably protect any facility from airborne attacks.
byKey.67499d0eeca8acb2d2061639 Description: A letter from the BTR driver. Apparently, the information inside could put serious pressure on Skier.
byKey.67499b3eeca8acb2d2061636 Description: From the sounds of it, the case is filled with something heavy like OFZ shells or other munitions.
byKey.67499d2c69a58fceba104a43 Description: From the sounds of it, the case is filled with something heavy like OFZ shells or other munitions.
byKey.675f7acc4076a741a3061566 Description: A stack of documents with data on TerraGroup shipments. Contains reports on completed and planned shipments.
byKey.675f7b168d28a25ec7007dbb Description: It looks like this journal was used by the entire loading crew to mark all the loads that had already been completed. How could the foreman make any sense of this handwriting?
byKey.675f80d4fe1b59cf490d3527 Description: The box is sealed, but judging by the sounds inside, it contains the tools Mechanic was looking for.
byKey.675f7f224076a741a3061568 Description: It's hard to believe this wallet is anything special to Skier. It's just an old, shabby wallet. How has it not disintegrated yet?
byKey.679b9a1a4e4ed4b3b40ae5c2 Description: Meetings, facilities, and other notes from Knossos senior manager are noted in the diary. If you study them, you can get at least a rough summary of the company's facilities.
byKey.679b98e429acd1f2f60985a3 Description: A chemical container with a thick, murky liquid inside. Only a lunatic like Sanitar would want to study something like this.
byKey.679b9aa490622daf9708da73 Name: VPX Flash Storage Module marked Group #3
byKey.679b9aa490622daf9708da73 Description: The VPX Flash Storage Module (FSM) provides high-performance, high-capacity, solid-state SATA storage with AES-256 bit encryption using an Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC). Judging by the marking, it contains data on the focus group experiments and research.
byKey.679b998180a165f7a40b4c2c Description: A videotape with traces of blood and the words “Slaughter”. The owner of the tape hardly felt sympathy for his victims.
byKey.683ed6aed885538c4102d8c8 Description: A 24 inch barrel for the AK-50 sniper rifle.
byKey.683ed6c2e4b1dd7ec4069dc8 Description: A receiver dust cover for the AK-50 sniper rifle.

byKey.68666482abad2f29b00aab57 Description: A broken generic phone, nothing out of the ordinary. However it might help to find Mechanic's acquaintance.
byKey.6866663e022740fabd074ef2 Description:
An unremarkable diary, there are hundreds of those in Tarkov. But don't judge a book by its cover: this particular one contains many dangerous secrets.

The first page has a table of contents:
• Update
• Notes 
• Highlights
• Encrypt
• Agenda 
• Ruminates
• Drafts
byKey.687502c4660d147e2502a94f Description: A simple disk with a handwritten note that this is the second version, the final one. Finally you can go through the whole game all the way to the end. Gotta write a review later!

Escalation in Tarkov

The military conflict in Tarkov continues to escalate. Eyewitnesses remaining in the city report increasing clashes between BEAR and USEC units. UN forces and the Russian Armed Forces are cordoning off dangerous areas, but these zones are growing, and according to unconfirmed reports, high-level discussions are already underway regarding a potential full lockdown of the city.

Both PMC groups likely still maintain their supply channels for weapons and personnel, which is why almost no one is willing to make optimistic forecasts. Evacuation of civilians is difficult, and both sides are organizing humanitarian aid drops to help local residents hold out until safe corridors open.

Amid the crisis, local criminal groups are also becoming more active. In some cases, these groups manage to seize weapons and take control of parts of the city. Currently, three such areas are known.

In the city center, the criminal gang of a former entrepreneur, known by the alias "Kaban", has established a fortified base in the former LexOs car dealership. According to recent data, PMC units have unsuccessfully attempted to dislodge the gang several times. An anonymous source told the editorial team that Kaban possesses samples of heavy weaponry that cannot even be obtained on the black market. Some experts suggest a possible connection between Kaban and the nonprofit organization "Forward Movement", which was previously linked in a high-profile case involving deputy minister of economy Yaroslav Shkurenko and the criminal authority nicknamed Chepyga.

Near the customs terminal, the "Zavodskoy" gang, previously involved in petty thefts in the district, has been spotted. Eyewitnesses report ongoing gunfire in that area.

EMERCOM units were forced to abandon evacuation points near the "Ultra" mall due to increased attacks by armed groups that took control of one floor of the mall. EMERCOM tents at the nearby highway interchange are no longer safe.

EMERCOM recommendations remain the same: first, find a secure shelter and wait for evacuation there, provide aid to the wounded if possible, and avoid venturing onto city streets. We hope that UN forces and the Russian Armed Forces will take more decisive measures to cool the conflict in Tarkov and will continue reporting all important developments.

Purpose and characteristics
Item #1156 — an aerosol augmenter of radio-frequency electromagnetic emission (RF-EMI), designed to neutralize enemy electronic equipment over a large area. The item can be used on its own or as the warhead component of delivery systems (tactical, operational-tactical, and medium range).
Weight: 37.080 kg
Dimensions: 2500*800*800
Effect radius: 15 to 40 km depending on medium density
Activation:
1. Remote initiation using a timed/distance fuze (up to 200m) /
2. Remote initiation via radio communication (within the radio’s operational range)


General design
The shock-wave emitter operates by means of spherically symmetric compression of the electromagnetic field. The fuze consists of a magnetic system that directs magnetic poles to the center of a sphere formed by two intersecting magnetic flux rings.

Inside the magnetic flux sphere is a detonation distributor, made from a plastic sphere with 45 channels filled with an initiating high explosive (lead azide was tested). The channel system ensures simultaneous arrival of the detonation wave at the main explosive charge.

At the center of the detonation distributor is the main explosive charge (tested mixtures included trotyl-hexogen combinations, octogen, and tetryl). Embedded in the center of the main charge is a cesium iodide single crystal treated with mixture #3012.


Features
Using spherically symmetric compression of the electromagnetic field together with treatment of the cesium iodide single crystal with mixture #3012 provides a significant increase in pulse efficiency compared to known EMI weapon prototypes. Measurements taken during testing showed retention of 40 to 50% of the explosive energy.

– According to our information, Cobalt has been facing difficulties integrating into Tarkov’s energy infrastructure. Is that true?

– I wouldn’t put it that way. Yes, innovation requires significant energy resources, and our facilities are no exception. Some of our projects demand power plants that simply don’t exist in the region. But the company’s development strategy already includes the construction of next-generation power stations. And we’ve made progress – just two days ago we, hm, reached an agreement with Yaroslav Grigorievich! (editor’s note: Deputy Minister of Economy Shkurenko Y. G.) In the future, Cobalt will bring light to many citizens of Tarkov, and today’s difficulties have only highlighted a problem in the city that we intend to solve.

– So you see the problem as lying with the city, not the costs of your projects? Our data suggests Tarkov has never suffered from a power shortage.

– Are you asking whether our projects can improve the city’s situation? That’s a great question! And I’ll say this: one of the key reasons for choosing this site was its potential for developing energy infrastructure, and in that regard, Tarkov certainly has room to grow. You have to understand – it’s not about what Tarkov looks like now, it’s about what it will become with us.

– Speaking of innovation. We’ve calculated that even taken together, all of Cobalt’s public projects don’t consume that much electricity. It seems Cobalt is planning to increase the city’s power load several times over for a project the people of Tarkov know nothing about. How do you comment on that?

– We understand the public’s concern and appreciate the interest in our work! But right now, even a small leak could seriously affect the development process. The walls have ears, right? Too much openness could harm not only Cobalt, but also Russia’s position on the international market. But getting back to Tarkov and its energy infrastructure – we’ve already reached a compromise with the local authorities. Until our new plants are operational, we’ll be "staying over" at state-owned facilities. For now, we’ll have to squeeze into city power plant buildings, but once our stations come online, the people of Tarkov will forget about power shortages entirely.

– Well, we’re intrigued by Cobalt’s new project and look forward to hearing more. This has been Yuri Belogorov from Lights of Tarkov, and Nikolay Tretyakov, NGO Cobalt representative in Tarkov.

PURPOSE AND CHARACTERISTICS

Automated Radio Relay Service (ARRS) is a system composed of multiple surveillance and communications agents, designed to prepare and control protocols Fortress, Spark, and Obelisk. The list of permitted protocols may be expanded.

The ARRS system is fully autonomous and can operate without external power sources, including under protocol Twilight. If an ARRS agent is disconnected from the network, each module can continue recording for up to 2 years and retain stored data for up to 10 years.

The system supports expansion with additional ARRS modules and automatic updates.

Each ARRS module is equipped with a unique security system (MOU-73S) capable of completely locking the module. Access to a module is possible only with a unique identifier embedded in the senior operator’s key.



GENERAL DESIGN

The ARRS system has no single control center. Each ARRS module locally stores the following data:
1) Scripts required for the module’s autonomous operation
2) Scripts for verifying user access level and transmitting data according to protocol The Eye (HGL-01E)
3) Archive of recordings for the entire observation history
4) Scripts to initiate protocol Warden (JKL-13R)

Module preparation and assembly are carried out according to the instructions described in Appendix 17 (TUR-09L).

ARRS modules operate on a closed infrastructure. The model, methods, and architectural requirements are described in Appendix 21 (UTE-99Y).

̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲ ̲


The Will of Chance

Greetings to all survivors. I don’t know what I’d do without being able to talk to you. Sometimes it even feels like the old world never existed, as if everything collapsed into this closed-off city where each of us has just one mission – to make it through to tomorrow.

But today, I want to share a story that gives me hope for a better outcome. Maybe it will help you too.

Yesterday I went to check on a wounded friend and met a gloomy, withdrawn BEAR sitting in Therapist’s recovery room, clutching a USEC patch in his hands. At first glance, it seemed obvious: a trophy from a heavy fight where he lost a comrade. He’d avenged him, sure, but that hadn’t brought him peace. So there he sat, angry at himself for not being able to double-tap that USEC in time. Still, I decided to strike up a conversation, and from his first words, I realized all my guesses were wrong.

This BEAR had been scouting a new route to TerraGroup’s underground lab when his squad discovered an elevator shaft in critical condition. They managed to reach the complex through it and complete their mission, but on the way back, Raiders pinned them down hard.

During the retreat, the shaft collapsed, burying the entire team except for our guy. He himself was pinned against a wall by a support beam. The surface was just a couple hundred meters away, but without help, he had no chance of making it out alive. So he decided to hold on as long as he could.

Two days later, he heard footsteps approaching. He recognized English speech, but by then he couldn’t even hold his pistol, let alone put up a fight. He saw a flashlight beam sweep the tunnel ahead and braced himself for the end.

But instead of a gunshot, he heard a safety click, followed by careful steps. The newcomer wasn’t an enemy, but an ally. The stranger helped him get free, but the effort triggered heavy bleeding that his exhausted body couldn’t handle.

What happened next he remembers only in fragments, drifting in and out of consciousness. All his strength went into holding onto that USEC, and at some point, he accidentally tore the patch off the stranger’s shoulder.

He woke up in Therapist’s care, never finding out who had pulled him from the rubble. All he had left was the patch, which he now keeps with him.

We often convince ourselves that we’re in control, but most things around us are shaped by forces we can’t predict – a lucky weather break during retreat, a weapon jam in the enemy’s hands, or the will of a random passerby.

To everyone reading this: I wish you hope for a better outcome, even when everything seems set against you.

That’s all for now. Stay alive till tomorrow.

Down the Untrodden Paths

I welcome my readers once again. The Contract Wars have forever changed Tarkov’s landscape, and knowing the terrain often means the difference between life and death. Many turn to Jaeger for help, but the forester’s experience is of little use in urban areas or on the outskirts.

Some of you may have heard of the Mushroom Picker who roams across the city, though few have ever met him in person. At one point, both the military and the Scavs were hunting the reclusive old man. It’s said the Mushroom Picker has no ties to TerraGroup and has never even held a weapon. Still, many would pay a fortune to have him on their side.

That’s because the old man knows routes and passages that no one has walked, even in peaceful times. Somehow, the Mushroom Picker manages to avoid army checkpoints, not to mention Scav camps. With knowledge like that, he can seriously affect the balance of power in Tarkov.

Yet no one has ever truly understood his motives or goals. The more devout citizens like to tell stories of his night-time encounters with witnesses of the Arrival. To be honest, I don’t rule anything out anymore.

Despite his murky nature, the Mushroom Picker sometimes appears to those who’ve lost their way. I personally know several people, and they share nothing in common: he’s helped mercenaries from both PMCs, civilians, and even Scavs.

Whatever moral compass guides this eccentric wanderer, his help is not something one can count on. A meeting with the Mushroom Picker only happens when he wills it.

That’s all for now. Stay alive till tomorrow.

During the reporting period 14 groups of test subjects were examined at the site. Each group contained between 5 and 25 people depending on the experimental conditions. Some experiments could not be carried out due to the site’s limited capabilities. Group 9 was redirected to Site Theta because of the risk of contamination and the poor containment of the “Labyrinth” premises. Group 1 had to be neutralized entirely for similar reasons.

However, most experiments proved effective and provided the material and conclusions required by the laboratories and other test sites. Studies were conducted on effects on the human body and on expanding physical capabilities. Work proceeded along three directions:
1) Increasing organism endurance under various conditions.
2) Testing the effects of experimental biological compounds on the human body.
3) Developing compounds capable of affecting the human mental state.



Increasing organism endurance under various conditions.
During the study, subjects were placed in various conditions (food deprivation, prolonged confinement in a restricted space, blood loss exceeding 20/30/40% of total blood volume, burns with ITP from 50 to 95 points, acute and subacute intoxication).

Compounds SJ6, eTG-c, and SJ1 demonstrated significant effectiveness in stabilizing condition and activating the organism’s reserve resources in poisoning of varying severity and intoxication in the presence of open wounds. Compounds SJ15 and M.U.L.E. demonstrated high effectiveness under favorable conditions and increased subjects’ activity periods by 47–60%.

As a result of the studies, eTG-c, SJ6, and SJ15 are recommended for further iteration and development. The lack of professional training among test subjects negatively affected research results, therefore when used on trained combat personnel, the projected effect may reach higher results. Field testing is required.

Testing the effects of experimental biological compounds on the human body.
Extensive testing of already developed combat stimulants was carried out according to the established plan.

Compounds P22 and M.U.L.E. exhibited critical side effects with regular use. Subjects were diagnosed with muscle tissue atrophy and, in isolated cases, paralysis or necrosis of individual muscles (3% of subjects). The research group associates these effects with excessive wear of muscle tissue and the organism’s inability to recover after such pressure. It is recommended to develop an advanced version of these compounds in which, after administration of the functional composition, a restorative mixture is also administered to replace expended physiological resources.

Development of a new formulation of the compound Zagustin continues. Formulations that thinned the blood immediately after the action of the primary mixture were tested, but subjects exhibited symptoms similar to hemophilia. In parallel a Zagustin-based compound with reduced effect on profibrinolysin activators is being developed. Report


On Jan. 2, the Bogatyr squad carried out a hostage evacuation from the Tarbank branch on Korablestroiteley Street. The enemy had taken up firing positions on the 1st and 2nd floors. Hostages were sheltered in the reception area on the 1st floor.

A direct assault was ruled out to minimize risk to the hostages. I decided to clear the building with two teams. The first team (call signs: Moreman, Kaskad) ascended to the 2nd floor using climbing gear and engaged the enemy utilizing smoke grenades.

Meanwhile, the main assault team (call signs: Voevoda, Taran, Vityaz), under sniper overwatch (call sign: Strelets), attacked the enemy on the 1st floor and extracted the hostages. The operation was completed swiftly, no hostages were injured. Fourteen targets were neutralized, presumably members of Kaban's criminal gang. No casualties in the Bogatyr squad.

The operation drew attention from nearby USEC forces and local civilians, and the squad had to repel enemy attacks twice during the withdrawal. After handing over the freed hostages to Russian Armed Forces, the Bogatyr squad will relocate from its previous bases to the Carousel outpost to await further instructions.

Bogatyr squad commander

SITUATION REPORT

Armed clashes between criminal groups in the Tarkov suburbs have become increasingly frequent in recent weeks. This morning, the Ministry of Internal Affairs for Tarkov issued a press release following multiple citizen inquiries.

While the investigation remains ongoing, ministry representatives confirmed a number of established facts regarding criminal activity in the Tarkov and Norvinsk districts.

According to available data, the recent crime wave is tied to escalating conflict between several organizations, one of which, led by the crime boss known as Arseny Petrovich Chepygin, is rapidly expanding its influence.

Chepygin’s group has grown more aggressive over the past six months, consolidating control over new territories. The reasons for this sudden power shift remain unclear, but it’s evident that without serious backing, the gang could not have achieved such success.

The question of who this mysterious “investor” might be, and what their motives are, remains open. We’ll continue to follow the situation closely.

12.11.
Got out of Stockholm without any trouble. But during the layover the whole place turned into a complete fucking shitshow. Not only did they pull the entire crew off the ship and slow all work onboard to a crawl, they wouldn’t even let us stand nearby. And for what? With paranoia like that no wonder Terragroup rotates crews on the icebreaker so often. Short-ass contracts, all these fucked protocols, all this secrecy bullshit… nobody’d put up with this crap if the pay wasn’t insane.

And I even managed to sneak a look at the loading op. They got people running back and forth nonstop and all they’re loading is crates full of electronics. Even the dockworkers are their own guys. Nobody GIVES A FUCK about your electronics, we’ve carried worse at sea! Arrogant fucking asshole fucks.

20.11
Made it to Tarkov, which means Saint Petersburg’s close now. Just hope we don’t get stuck here too like we did in Stockholm. Almost home.
byKey.69bb4558b44453acde02ebe7_Note_Page2_Text:
09.12
Wow what great fucking luck. They delayed the stopover while we were already approaching Tarkov, then canceled the whole thing completely. Heard something serious happened with Terragroup in the city, maybe even a shootout or some shit. If even half of it’s true, we’re gonna be sitting here for a long damn time.

15.01
Knew right away this was going to turn into a disaster… We’re fucked, royally. Orders came down from above to drop anchor and wait for further instructions and meanwhile everything in Tarkov just keeps getting worse. Alex says UN troops’ll enter the city soon and everything’ll calm down. Yeah, sure. Fucking sure it will…

3.06
Still no orders. Comms started acting up too. Usually at least you know when your contract ends, but here you just sit around losing your damn mind. Max’s family in Tarkov saw military vehicles in the streets. Maybe our guys’ll finally get shit under control??

Thought I’d never even find this notebook again. And sure as hell never thought I’d end up trapped on this goddamn icebreaker for years. Fucking blockade… And that bastard Altman deserves worse than death!

Yes the boys broke. We should’ve called for evacuation a long damn time ago! Maybe a year back those USECs still could’ve smuggled us across the cordon. Obvious enough command stopped giving a shit about us the second troops rolled into the city.

But no. Altman’s precious materials matter more than actual living people whose brains are already melting in this frozen hell!

VEIL (Vectorized Exo-atmospheric Intelligence Lattice) Satellite
Network Readiness


The project to establish the VEIL orbital satellite network has reached its final construction
stage. Integration of the satellites in the Lambda sector completed the orbital network,
providing full coverage of the northern regions of Europe and Asia as well as the entire
territories of both American continents.

Despite the project nearing completion, the suspension of TerraGroup’s public humanitarian
and scientific programs, as well as those of its subsidiaries related to ground and orbital
network infrastructure, is not recommended. At this stage it is essential to minimize
external attention from government authorities and the press. I recommend continuing all
projects regardless of the cost of these investments. All associated expenses will be
included in the VEIL project budget.

In its current configuration, the VEIL system allows interception of signals across its entire
coverage area and their seamless substitution, as well as the ability to simulate
transmissions from specific senders, including government agencies of individual countries.
In most sectors it is also possible to temporarily suppress any communications systems.
(Satellites in the Upsilon and Delta sectors are still undergoing modernization and currently
do not provide this capability.)

Separately addressing the concerns raised by Ms. McRory: detection of the network by
external means is practically impossible due to our modernization of the satellite hardware
and the integration of officially decommissioned satellites into the network.
Intelligence methods can only detect fragmented satellite coverage belonging to TerraGroup,
which is insufficient to raise suspicion among journalists or intelligence services.
Potential risks are associated only with TerraGroup’s public activities, particularly their abrupt
termination or deviations from declared plans for public scientific and humanitarian projects.

Integration of the ARRS network with VEIL is proceeding according to schedule. Only final
testing remains, after which system access and control of VEIL via ARRS terminals will be
possible using the appropriate access codes. Access codes will be distributed individually
through the VEIL system.

Immediately after full deployment, the project’s scientific team will be reassigned to the
development of the first prototypes of incoherent wireless transmission (IWT) equipment.

P. Wilson
